_note: Q-09 is the only endpoint in the API that is not JSON. It is a
multipart/form-data upload with a single part named `photo`; the
response is still the usual { success, data, error } envelope.
The bytes go straight to Cloudinary and never touch Postgres — only
the delivery URL is stored, on help_requests.image_url.
`image_url` and `has_photo` are returned on every request payload
(Q-02, Q-03, Q-04, P-01), so there is no image GET endpoint to call:
render image_url directly when has_photo is true.
The URL is public. Anyone holding it can fetch the photo, so it should

attach_photo.auth: senior, and only on their own request

parts.name: photo
parts.constraints: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp; 5 MB max

_error_shapes.400 NO_IMAGE: the part was missing or named something other than `photo`
_error_shapes.400 UPLOAD_FAILED: Cloudinary rejected the upload. Note this is reported as a client error although the cause is server-side
_error_shapes.404 NOT_FOUND: not the caller's request, or it does not exist — answered identically so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which ids are real
_error_shapes.409 INVALID_STATE: the request is cancelled or completed
_error_shapes.503 IMAGE_UPLOAD_UNAVAILABLE: the server has no Cloudinary credentials; the rest of the API is unaffected

_ordering: The photo cannot be part of the Q-01 create body: the request id is
not known until Q-01 has answered. Clients create the request first,
then upload with the returned request_id.
A failed upload does not roll the request back and must not trigger a
resend — resending trips BR-13 (one open request per senior) and would
tell a senior who has already been dispatched that they have a
duplicate. Report it in the UI and leave the request alone.
The ownership check runs before the body is read, so a rejected upload

request_with_photo.description: Need help buying groceries for the week

request_without_photo.description: Need a ride to the clinic for a check-up
